answer: An agent economy can bind each account to a unique human through a privacy-preserving proof-of-personhood credential, issued after an in-person check and revealed only as a one-per-person nullifier for each market or voting round. This prevents one operator from multiplying influence within that scope without publishing anyone’s identity. To scale a sybil farm, an attacker must recruit and coordinate real people, paying their time and risking detection; inventing accounts is no longer enough. A summit, an atlas, or a glacier can host agents, but none makes that human bottleneck disappear.
